title: Probabilistic mapping and image clustering for quantitative assessment of fluorescent protein localizations in Arabidopsis guard cells
protocol: Prepare the target stack image from the LIPS database.
Run the ImageJ software.
Open the target image using the "File-Open" option in ImageJ.
Draw the major stomatal pore line on the bright field image using the "Straight Line Selection Tool".
Copy the segmented straight line from the bright field image to the fluorescence images using the "Edit-Selection-Restore Selection" menu.
Rotate the fluorescence image using the "Plugins-kbi-Kbi_registration (mode: horizoner)" option.
Get the maximum intensity projection image using ImageJ menu “Image-Stacks-Z project…”.
Put a bounding box around the cell using the ImageJ tool bar menu “Rectangular Selection Tool”.
Crop the boxed cell region using the ImageJ menu “Image-Crop”.
If the pore is located in the upper half of the cropped image, rotate the image 180 degrees using the ImageJ menu “Image-Transform-Rotate…”.
Resize the images to the same size using the ImageJ menu “Image-Adjust-Size…”.
Run the ImageJ software.
Make a stack image using the ImageJ menu “Plugins-kbi-Kbi_StkJoin (mode: all axis: z)”.
Run the macro hig_Pdmapping.ijm.
Save the probability map image using the ImageJ menu “File-Save”.
Run the ‘ImageJ’ software.
Open the stack image of the probability maps using the ImageJ menu “File-Open”.
Shrink the image size using the ImageJ menu “Image-Adjust-Size…” to 70×27 pixels.
Run the macro hig_Lineprofile.ijm.
Save the raster-scanned intensity profiles as a csv file using the Results table menu “File-Save As…”.
Select 'sampleZ_featureCsv_patchImg' in the somMode drop-down list.
Load the csv file of the raster-scanned intensity profiles.
Observe the SOM image.
In cases where multiple images are allocated to the same node in the SOM, allocate these images to the next slice of the stack image.
